Raster data

Getting raster data

For this assignment, we will use the municipality boundary and the housing price data we have already used in the last assignment.

We will complement these data with two raster datasets:

  • Visit https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/geodata/height.html and download the Digital Height Model 25/200 for Switzerland.

    • Read the file DHM200.xyz as a raster. Check its CRS and assign a value if needed. If this information is missing, retrieve the relevant CRS in the documentation and assign to your object using the function crs(x) <- value. Use an EPSG code as a proj4string definition with "+init=epsg:MY_NUMBER" (so the command is: crs(x) <- "+init=epsg:MY_NUMBER"). You will probably get warnings while assigning the CRS. This is due to a migration from proj4string towards PROJ6 standards. You can ignore these warnings.
# Load the file DHM200.xyz from the Digital Height Model 25/200 for Switzerland
# Assign the correct CRS if needed
dhm <- raster("/Users/zitian/Downloads/data/DHM200.xyz")
crs(dhm) <- "+init=epsg:21781"
## Warning in CPL_crs_from_input(x): GDAL Message 1: +init=epsg:XXXX syntax is
## deprecated. It might return a CRS with a non-EPSG compliant axis order.

  • Visit https://map.geo.admin.ch and downloard the daytime road traffic noise exposure from the Federal Office for the Environment.

    • Read the file StrassenLaerm_Tag.tif (that is in the folder STRASSENLAERM_Tag that you downloaded) as a raster. Check its CRS and assign a value if needed.
# Load the file StrassenLaerm_Tag.tif
noise_raster <- raster("/Users/zitian/Downloads/data (1)/STRASSENLAERM_Tag/STRASSENLAERM_Tag.tif")

Raster extraction

  • Assign to the housing price data the level of noise exposure for that location.
# Step 1: reproject the vector object to the CRS of the raster datahousing_data_sf <- st_as_sf(
housing_data_sf <- st_as_sf(
  housing_data,
  coords = c("longitude2", "latitude2"),  
  crs = 4326                             
)
housing_data_sf <- st_transform(housing_data_sf, crs(noise_raster))

# Step 2: extract the values for the corresponding raster's cell
housing_data_sp <- as(housing_data_sf, "Spatial")
housing_data$noise_exposure <- extract(noise_raster, housing_data_sp)

Rasterization

  • Rasterize the dataset on housing prices to show the average price per square meters (a_brutm_m2) for grids of 1,000m x 1,000m
    • Create a raster template using housing price data.
    • Convert (a_brutm_m2) into numeric using the functions as.numeric(as.character(x))
# Convert factor variable into numeric
housing_data_sf$a_brutm_m2 <- as.numeric(as.character(housing_data_sf$a_brutm_m2))
# Create raster template
bbox <- st_bbox(housing_data_sf)  
raster_template <- raster(xmn = bbox["xmin"], 
                          xmx = bbox["xmax"], 
                          ymn = bbox["ymin"], 
                          ymx = bbox["ymax"], 
                          res = 1000, 
                          crs = st_crs(housing_data_sf)$proj4string)
# Rasterize 
r_price <- rasterize(housing_data_sp, raster_template, field = "a_brutm_m2", fun = mean)
# Plot
plot(r_price, main = "Average Price per m² (Rasterized)")

# Interactive version of the rasterized average price map
# Reproject r_price to WGS84 for interactive mapping
r_price_wgs <- projectRaster(r_price, crs = CRS("+init=epsg:4326"))
# Create a color palette for the raster values
pal_price <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", values(r_price_wgs), na.color = "transparent")
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addRasterImage(r_price_wgs, colors = pal_price, opacity = 0.8) %>%
  addLegend(pal = pal_price, values = values(r_price_wgs), title = "Average Price per m²") %>%
  setView(lng = 8.2275, lat = 46.8182, zoom = 8)

Spatial vectorization

  • Create contour lines for 250, 500, 1000 and 2000 m.a.s.l for the digital height model. Use a mask to select only the data for Switzerland.
    • Create a polygon for Switzerland based on the municipality boundary data. Remove the z geometry using st_zm() and reproject the data.
    • Store the polygon as Spatial object (with as(x,"Spatial")).
    • Create a mask for the the raster data
    • Create contour lines for the desired levels (look at ?rasterToContour to create the desired lines).
# Create a polygon for Switzerland
swiss_polygon <- st_union(municipality)
swiss_polygon <- st_zm(swiss_polygon)
swiss_polygon <- st_transform(swiss_polygon, crs = st_crs(dhm))
swiss_polygon_sp <- as(swiss_polygon, "Spatial")
# Create a mask for raster data
dhm_mask <- mask(dhm, swiss_polygon_sp)
# Create contour lines
contour_levels <- c(250, 500, 1000, 2000)
contours <- rasterToContour(dhm_mask, levels = contour_levels)
  • Create a hillshade layer to use as a basemap for the noise data
# Create a hill shade layer and mask cells outside Switzerland
slope <- terrain(dhm, opt = "slope")
aspect <- terrain(dhm, opt = "aspect")
hillshade <- hillShade(slope, aspect, angle = 40, direction = 270)
hillshade <- mask(hillshade, swiss_polygon_sp)
# Plot the hillshade layer and noise data
plot(
  noise_raster,
  main = "Hillshade with Noise Data",
  legend.shrink = 0.8,
  axis.args = list(cex.axis = 0.7, las = 1)
)
